name: Shimri
overview: Shimri was a male Levite, specifically a descendant of Elizaphan, belonging to the Kohathite clan which traces its lineage through Uzziel and Kohath, sons of Levi. His heritage places him within the tribe responsible for particular religious duties in Israel. This lineage is explicitly noted in 2 Chronicles 29:13.
namesAndTitles: The name Shimri means 'YHWH guards, preserves,' reflecting a theologically significant meaning rooted in the Hebrew understanding of divine protection. This proper name is not indicated to have been given directly by God, but it carries a clear spiritual connotation as recorded in 2 Chronicles 29:13.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Shimri as a descendant of Elizaphan, establishing a direct familial link within the Levite tribe. Beyond this explicit relationship, no additional family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Shimri's importance in the biblical narrative is tied to his Levitical heritage and role within the Kohathite clan, which had specific responsibilities in the worship and service of God. Being a descendant of Elizaphan situates Shimri within a key priestly lineage, emphasizing the continuity of God's ordained service through the tribe of Levi. His mention in 2 Chronicles 29:13 highlights his participation in the restoration of proper worship under King Hezekiah, underscoring the faithfulness of God's people in maintaining covenantal duties.
